thesis: TSMC is the indispensable node of the entire AI economy: Q1 2026 revenue $35.9B at a 66.2% gross margin with profit +58% y/y, HPC/AI now 61% of revenue, 2026 guidance raised to >30% USD growth, and every major AI chip designer (Nvidia, AMD, Apple, Broadcom, Marvell) required to migrate to its 2nm node in 2027 - with wafer prices rising. After a +91% twelve-month run to ~$437 (~33x trailing), the market has substantially priced this in, while the two structural discounts - Taiwan geopolitics and a $52-56B capex cycle with mounting overseas-fab costs - have not gone away. Q2 earnings land July 16.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results July 16, 2026: guidance $39-40.2B revenue, GM 65.5-67.5%
2nm (N2) risk production 2H 2026, high-volume 2027 - with all top customers migrating and wafer prices rising in 2027
FY2026 guidance already raised to >30% USD revenue growth on 'extremely robust' AI demand
CoWoS/advanced packaging capacity expansions serving AI accelerator backlog
Any pricing announcements confirming 2027 wafer-price increases
risk_factors: Taiwan geopolitical risk: unhedgeable, structural, and the reason the multiple has always carried a discount - a discount the +91% run has largely erased
Margin sustainability: 2nm ramp depreciation, overseas-fab cost premiums (Arizona/Japan/Germany), and customer order timing all pressure the 66% GM
Capex $52-56B (upper end) suppresses near-term FCF like the rest of the AI complex
Supply-chain exposure flagged to Middle East disruptions (energy, helium, hydrogen)
AI-capex digestion would hit the 61%-of-revenue HPC segment directly

q1_2026_revenue.note: +6.4% q/q; GM 66.2%; profit +58% y/y; HPC 61% of revenue; advanced nodes 74% of wafer revenue
